content:
RESOLVED to approve the following:
 

a.    
the proposed financial and officer support for Neighbourhood
Planning groups from UDC as described by this report, which
consists of:
i.               
£5,000 grant to Larger Villages who are proposing
non-strategic housing allocations (part of which will fund an
SEA)
ii.             
‘In-kind’ officer support (to an approximate value of
£5,000 in officer time) for specific technical support to
Larger Villages who are proposing non-strategic housing
allocations
iii.            
General Officer advice/ support for the Larger Villages (as
above)
iv.            
Half a day per week funding for the Rural Community Council for
Essex (RCCE) to enable them to support up to six Smaller Villages
(total £14,700 per annum)
v.             
General officer advice/ support for other communities who may wish
to pursue Neighbourhood Planning, subject to availability of
resources.

 

b.    
A proposed hybrid approach Note to supporting Neighbourhood
Planning with UDC Officers primarily supporting the Larger Villages
who are proposing non-strategic housing allocations, and RCCE
primarily supporting Smaller Villages), albeit with realistic
limits for how many communities can be supported at any one
time.
 

c.    
To agree to the annual review of the Council’s approach/
protocol for supporting Neighbourhood Planning.
topline: The UK council has decided to approve financial and officer support for Neighbourhood Planning groups.

purpose:
To respond to the letter from the Minister of
State for Local Government and Homelessness regarding the proposal
to postpone May 2026 elections.
content:
RESOLVED to respond to the letter from the
Minister of State for Local Government and Homelessness regarding
the postponement of elections in May 2026, as per the letter
appended.

The Minister of State for Local
Government and Homelessness has invited responses
from Council Leaders on the potential postponement of
local elections scheduled to take place in the Essex area
in May 2026.  
 
The Council strongly opposes
any further delay to local elections on the basis that
this would represent weakening the Democratic
Mandate, further delay the implementation of new electoral
boundaries leaving residents in Uttlesford under
represented at the county level, and that the Council is
confident in the capability of its officers to deliver upcoming
elections alongside Local Government
Reorganisation.   
 
The Secretary of State has
adopted
a locally-led approach and advises that a
decision will be delivered as soon as possible.
topline: The Leader of the Council has decided to oppose the postponement of local elections in May 2026.

content:
RESOLVED to approve the response to the Local
Government Reorganisation Consultation as appended.

To respond to the Government’s
consultation on the future of local government in Essex.
 
The government believes reorganising councils
into a smaller number of  single-tier unitary councils will deliver
stronger local councils equipped to deliver high quality public
services.
 
The consultation seeks views on the four
proposals received from councils for unitary local government.
 
The government expects to set out their
decision on which to proposal to implement in March 2026.
 
The council is looking to respond to the
consultation before the deadline on 11 January 2026.

None.

None.
topline: The Leader of the Council has decided to approve the response to the Local Government Reorganisation Consultation in Essex.

content:
RESOLVED to approve the list of successful
projects agreed by the selection panel as listed in Appendix
1. 

The one-off grant was initially launched on 14
January and applications closed midday on 21 February 2025. 
Applications were assessed by a cross-party working group of
members with officer support on Monday 31 March 2025.
 
A total of £47,180.66 grant funding was
awarded for 2025-26 and agreed by an Executive Decision published
on 9 April 2025.  It was agreed that the remaining budget of
£35,819.34 would be readvertised later in the year, using the
same criteria, and would not support applications for projects in
receipt of funding in the previous round.  
 
The one-off funding was reopened on 16 June
for new applications and closed on 29 August 2025.  A Panel of
cross-party members met on 29 September to assess the grant
applications.

None.
